description: The code logs raw exception details from Azure OpenAI client failures. Exception messages may contain sensitive operational details such as endpoint information, request metadata, model deployment names, or other internal error context. If logs are accessible to unauthorized users, this can aid reconnaissance or leak sensitive information.
recommendation: Avoid logging raw exception messages directly. Log a generic error message and capture detailed exception data only in secured debug logs with proper redaction and access controls.
name: Information exposure through exception logging

vulnerability: Information exposure through logging of internal file paths
description: The application logs every processed file path during repository scanning. File paths can reveal internal project structure, module names, or sensitive naming conventions. If logs are exposed to unauthorized users, this information can aid reconnaissance and facilitate targeted attacks.
recommendation: Avoid logging full internal file paths at info level. Log only high-level progress metrics or sanitized relative identifiers, and restrict detailed path logging to secured debug logs.
name: Information exposure through logging of internal file paths

vulnerability: Sensitive information exposure through console output
description: The code prints the full list of discovered vulnerabilities to standard output. Vulnerability records may include file names, line numbers, and code snippets, which can expose sensitive source code and security weaknesses if console output is captured by logs, CI/CD systems, or shared terminals.
recommendation: Do not print raw vulnerability details to stdout in production. Send results to a secured storage location, redact code snippets where possible, and restrict access to detailed scan outputs.
name: Sensitive information exposure through console output

vulnerability: Potential source code exfiltration to external LLM service
description: The scanner reads local source files and sends their full contents to an LLM through gpt_client for analysis. If the configured model endpoint is external or insufficiently controlled, sensitive source code, secrets embedded in files, proprietary logic, or internal paths may be disclosed to a third party. This creates a substantial data exposure risk, especially when scanning production or private repositories.
recommendation: Use a trusted, access-controlled LLM deployment with appropriate data processing guarantees. Minimize data sent to the model, redact secrets before transmission, obtain explicit approval for external processing, and enforce network and tenant restrictions for the LLM endpoint.
name: Potential source code exfiltration to external LLM service
